# Top Power BI and Microsoft Fabric consultants in Adelaide

For operational reporting and data warehousing, I’d shortlist a mix of **specialist Microsoft data consultancies and larger Fabric implementation partners**\. The key is to find a team that can do more than build attractive dashboards: they should be able to integrate source systems, engineer a reliable data warehouse, establish consistent KPIs, and deliver maintainable Power BI reporting.

Based on the available company profiles and published service information, these are the strongest candidates to investigate in Adelaide and South Australia. This is a practical shortlist, not a definitive ranking of independently verified project outcomes.

## Recommended shortlist

![Lobster Data Platform Reviews 2026: Details, Pricing, & Features | G2](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/L8zklLkuC9GWhHkLhkN1VfUBWff8KGam63Vi-9q1Oxv9Cb0-8-H3IP43qAAsSKNnPgIK4R1yPiJI01WkwcD2zYRvaDh78rDRJO8-cvvXKVwy0Ntbkk0JfYMabIMhP59XcnLa8eWp15iZ_CgHc4yfgjpCMecbGuSPY-oMEB-Ms0lxuAgmB9sUuhNA6DQOqUMD?purpose=fullsize)

(Best local specialist)

Kelly Broekstra brings data warehouse architecture and Power BI development experience. This is a particularly strong candidate if your reporting problems start with data quality, database design, or inconsistent figures. ## Which would I contact first?

| Your main requirement | My first call | Why |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Existing reports are slow, unreliable, or disagree | LobsterPot Solutions | Strong SQL Server and data warehouse expertise |
| You want to implement Microsoft Fabric | Agile Insights | Dedicated Fabric architecture and migration capability |
| You need practical operational KPI reporting | SFW | Established BI, reporting, and performance management focus |
| You need better data governance and business alignment | Dayta Darta | Combines strategy, governance, operational analytics, and integration |
| Reporting spans ERP, finance, and planning | Professional Advantage | Broader business systems and Microsoft analytics capability |


These are fit-based recommendations drawn from published capabilities, rather than a verified ranking of customer satisfaction or delivery quality.

## What to ask before engaging a consultant

For your use case, I would ask each shortlisted firm to demonstrate\:

1. **End-to-end delivery\:** A comparable project covering source-system integration, warehouse or lakehouse design, semantic models, and Power BI dashboards.
2. **Operational reporting\:** Examples involving daily or near-real-time KPIs, exceptions, service levels, productivity, inventory, or similar operational measures.
3. **Microsoft Fabric expertise\:** Named delivery staff with relevant Fabric engineering and analytics experience, including DP-700 and DP-600 certifications where applicable.
4. **Data governance\:** How they establish common KPI definitions, data-quality checks, access controls, and a single trusted version of the numbers.
5. **Ongoing ownership\:** Documentation, monitoring, performance tuning, training, and support after go-live.

Ask for two relevant client references, an indicative budget, and a proposed first-phase deliverable before committing to a large implementation.

## My recommendation

I would start with **LobsterPot Solutions and Agile Insights**, then compare their proposals with **SFW or Dayta Darta** if local hands-on delivery and operational reporting are your priorities.

One important distinction: if your objective is primarily reliable operational reporting, you may not need to migrate everything to Fabric immediately. A well-designed SQL warehouse and governed Power BI semantic model may be sufficient; Fabric becomes more compelling when you need broader data integration, scalable engineering, or a unified analytics platform.

**One question that would help me narrow this to the best two or three consultants\:** Are you mainly looking to improve an existing Power BI/SQL Server environment, or are you planning a new Microsoft Fabric data warehouse from scratch?
